correctness.rationale: The generating polynomial gives every orthogonal ANOVA component with correct coefficient normalization. Singular Lebesgue/Dirac faces are pairwise mutually singular, so total variation adds. Positive-probability rare-event embeddings give a rigorous lower bound on the L∞ norm; self-adjointness gives the L1 dual norm. Joint Newton-identity and CLT convergence supplies the shifted probabilists-Hermite normalization, and L2 bounds justify passing absolute moments. Deterministic alternating-binomial dominance supplies the m>>sqrt(n) limit. 440 finite exact-rational checks reproduce special cases and independent finite-atom approximants, but no infinite proof relies on them.

value.rationale: The exact sharp norm quantifies worst-case stability of a natural projection used for low-interaction approximation on heterogeneous continuous and binary data. At fixed k, the number of diffuse features needed to change the asymptotic stability class is exactly sqrt(n), and a shifted-Hermite formula describes the entire critical window. This is a substantive threshold and finite-parameter invariant, rather than a routine rewriting of a decomposition or a single isolated numeric case.
